key_insight: Stacking ensembles produced more accurate task-specific predictions than the multitask neural network for UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness, while MTNN offered stronger shared-learning generalization across related outputs.
engineering_relevance: For welding process optimization, these models can help estimate mechanical properties from shared process data, supporting faster parameter selection and improved weld quality control.
method: Compared a multitask neural network (shared hidden layers with task-specific outputs) against stacking ensemble learning.
Predicted three welding response variables: UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness.
Evaluated performance using RMSE and R² on the same dataset.
evidence_signal: MTNN achieved RMSE/R² of 0.1288/0.6724 for UTS, 0.0886/0.9215 for weld hardness, and 0.1125/0.8407 for HAZ hardness, while stacking improved to 0.0263/0.9863, 0.0467/0.9782, and 0.1109/0.8453, respectively.
watch_item: The study is based on a shared dataset, so model performance may depend on dataset size, feature quality, and how well the training data represent unseen welding conditions.
paper_title: A Comparative Analysis of Multitask Neural Networks and Stacking Ensemble Learning for Predicting UTS, Weld Hardness, and HAZ Hardness in Welding Applications
